d5d43627-da91-4ed9-9d68-7cfe36919a6b.description: Error ratio over 5m is above 14.4x the 1% error budget (fast burn); at this rate a 30-day budget lasts about 2 days.

facts.statement: Checkout revision 2 was created 20:36:37Z with change-cause 'payment client moved to port 9999'. Revision 1 is from 19:51:22Z.
The only pod-template diff between checkout revisions 1 and 2 is PAYMENT_ADDR: 'payment:8080' changed to 'payment:9999'.
Checkout's 20 sampled error traces all fail at PaymentService/Charge with 'dial tcp 10.96.32.3:9999: i/o timeout', propagating up to frontend /api/checkout as HTTP 500 / gRPC 13.
Checkout logs show a gRPC server stop and a config dump with paymentSvcAddr payment:9999 at 20:36:38Z. Checkout has no error-level log lines in 30 minutes.
Payment logs end at 20:36:38Z and show nothing afterward (info lines only).
Payment has one revision (19:51:22Z), no change cause, 1/1 available, and no warning events in the last 60 minutes.
All 18 flagd flags are off. No namespace crashloops or OOM kills occurred in the last 120 minutes.
Checkout's only erroring client span is PaymentService/Charge. Cart, currency, and product-catalog client spans show no errors, and there are no kafka, email, or shipping errors in 20:10-20:41.
Payment's server-side Charge errors were 0 from about 20:20 onward. The metrics report says Charge successes continued, which conflicts with the log silence after 20:36:38Z.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: kubectl get svc/endpoints payment; check the payment container listening port; roll back checkout to revision 1 and watch the checkout error ratio fall.
hypotheses.statement: Payment is not listening on 9999 and the checkout config is the fault. Confirm with payment's Service/endpoints and a container port check, and by rolling checkout back to PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Pull exception messages from payment Charge error spans for 20:10-20:20 and astronomy-db span errors and timings from product-catalog for 20:20-20:30.
hypotheses.statement: The 20:10-20:20 wave (payment Charge server errors plus product-catalog DB latency) is a separate, earlier issue, possibly in payment or the astronomy-db path.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check the timestamps of those payment spans against the 20:36:37Z change, and check for other payment span sources.
hypotheses.statement: The payment 'Invalid token' 422 error spans are stale or unrelated, since they conflict with payment's error-free logs and the dial timeout.

inferences.statement: The failure starts at the 20:36:37Z config rollout, about 3 minutes before the alert. The 1.0 error ratio at 20:43-20:44 fits all Charge calls failing against the wrong port.
Payment's silence after 20:36:38Z more likely reflects no traffic reaching it after the port change than a payment fault. Payment has no changes, warnings, or server-side errors of its own.

root_causes.cause: Bad config in checkout revision 2: PAYMENT_ADDR changed to payment:9999 (payment serves on 8080), so every PaymentService/Charge dial times out and PlaceOrder fails.

Earlier, separate slowdown (about 20:10-20:30): product-catalog GetProduct p95 reached about 9.5s, with astronomy-db spans up to 4.7s. Payment Charge errors also occurred 20:10-20:20. Neither has a confirmed cause, and both predate the config change.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout's fast ErrorBudgetBurn is most likely caused by its own config change: revision 2 (20:36:37Z) moved PAYMENT_ADDR from payment:8080 to payment:9999. Checkout's Charge calls now fail with dial i/o timeouts to 10.96.32.3:9999, which surface as HTTP 500/gRPC 13 at frontend. Payment shows no change or warnings of its own. Its logs go quiet at the same moment, which fits no traffic arriving. Not yet confirmed by payment-side listener or endpoint checks. A separate earlier wave (20:10-20:20, payment Charge errors plus product-catalog DB slowness) predates the change and is unexplained.
